title: Longest Consecutive Run
statement:
Find the longest set of values in an unsorted array that form an unbroken sequence of consecutive integers.

Contract
- `numbers` is non-null and may be empty; it is unsorted and may contain duplicates and any `int` values.
- A run is a set of distinct values `v, v + 1, ..., v + k - 1` that all appear somewhere in the array, in any positions. Return the largest run length `k`, or `0` for an empty array.
- `Integer.MAX_VALUE` and `Integer.MIN_VALUE` are not consecutive. Do not mutate `numbers`.

Examples
- `longestRun(new int[]{31, 8, 9, 30, 10, 32, 7})` returns `4`, from 7, 8, 9, 10.
- `longestRun(new int[]{5, 5, 5})` returns `1`.
- `longestRun(new int[0])` returns `0`.
hints: Sorting makes runs easy to see but costs more than linear time.
Put every value in a hash set. A value starts a run only when value - 1 is not in the set.

From each run start, count upward while the next value is present; each value is visited a constant number of times. Intended complexity: expected O(n) time and O(n) extra space, where n is the array length.
inputSyntax: Input: the array values, for example: [31, 8, 9, 30, 10, 32, 7]
